docs.title: Team Charter
docs.text:
From the ... which can be reviewed in "Appendix: Team Organization", the team's charter formed to be (showing ASU's Charter as an Example):

"ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves." (ASU's Charter)

Team 205 strives to create a culture of learning and team building that is illustrated by the successful completion of a marketable product meeting both educational and industry standards. We aim to grow personally and professionally into capable engineers in practical, technical, and social areas as we complete this course.

This Charter was created using the shared team goals for this course, as well as personal achievement aims of each member. Each member wants to develop something they can be proud of during the course as well as pick up and utilize necessary soft skills.

docs.title: Product Mission Statement
docs.text:
Describe the distilled purpose, function, or reason for your product to exist. From this form a team mission statement. Google's mission statement is:

"Google's mission is to organize the world's information and make it universally accessible and useful."

Team 205 designs precision robotic arm systems on the cutting edge of research technology and with cost efficiency as an important driver of success. By pushing the boundaries of robotic articulation and control, we deliver real-world value to clients, investors, and our community.

This mission statement was devised based on each of our shared hopes for the project, as well as how we would like our product to be recieved by patrons. We want to exemplify industry-standard technology and practices while also making sure the consumer is interested in the product.

docs.title: 1. XLUX Plant Soil Moisture Meter, for Indoor and Outdoor use, Battery-Free
docs.text:
• Price: $9.99

  • Vendor: Amazon

  • Description: The XLUX soil moisture meter is a reliable, easy to use tool that has been trusted since 2015. Its battery free probe measures moisture directly at the root level, while the large color coded display makes it easy to know when plants need water. The slim single probe design helps protect delicate roots and works well in different types of soil. It also includes a protective sleeve and stainless steel probe for durability.

docs.title: Positive Comments
docs.text: Voice of the Customer Restated Customer Need "I used to think I didn't have a green thumb, but over the years, I've tried and tried and YouTube has helped me learn a ton about caring for house plants. I now have a jungle in all three of my apartment rooms! I still have a mishap on occasion and honestly, it's usually about watering. I got tired of sticking my finger into dirt and started using a chopstick and checking to see if the bottom was moist. Meh. Then I figured I'd give this moisture meter a try. I'm so glad I did. It works really fast (instantly, really) and is so far very accurate. It seems well made and is sturdy. I expected more of a cheaply made item and I'm pleasantly surprised that this seems well made, especially for the low price. No batteries needed, which is so great. You don't need instructions - you just stick the probe into the bottom of your soil and it tells you the moisture content. You need to know the needs of each plant and water or not water based on the reading. The outer box comes with a guide on watering requirements for a large variety of plants, which would very helpful for beginners, but I know what each of my plants needs are, so I tossed the box. The probe is really long, so I'm happy about that feature. The probe is stainless and seems very durable. For $10, this is a must have if you are a plant owner. I wish I hadn't waited so long to pick this up!" 1.  The Product is durable (explicit) 2.  The Product is easy to understand (Explicit) 3.  The product is precise (explicit) Voice of the Customer Restated Customer Need "A very simple, basic product. No electronics, no moving parts. Just stick the metal rod into the plant soil (I usually check in two or three different spots) and it tells you on the dial how dry or moist the soil is. Some plants don't like the soil to ever get dry, other plants should definitely be allowed to dry out before being watered, so you need to know about your particular plant to fully benefit from this product. This moisture meter does prevent overwatering (which is a frequent cause of root rot and plant death). My only negative note is that the meter seems a bit fragile: I dropped one on the floor and although it looked fine, it stopped working (it would always read totally "dry"). I think the probe got disconnected from the meter inside the plastic top as a result of the impact sustained when it hit the floor. That's why I bought a second one." 1.  The Product has good ease of use (explicit) 2.  The product needs to be strong (latent) 3.  The product should display lots of information (latent) Voice of the Customer Restated Customer Need "Seems to work well, but I have noticed that after only a week theyre getting rusty. As long as the end probe holds up its not that big a deal. I like the orange color because I keep losing my green one. It does have a tendency to take a whie to register its final reading… for example, it normally measures higher moisture then settles in somewhere drier. Not a biggie, jsu not super responsive." 1.  The product needs to be rust resistant  (latent) 2.  The product works well (explicit) 3.  The product is simple (explicit)

docs.title: Project Objective
docs.text: This project aims to investigate and develop smart adaptive technologies, an improved user experience, better fit, improved product design, and product customization options for the next-generation AirPods. The target is to maintain global dominance in the wireless earphone market, drive up AirPod sales to 100 million+ units sold with a 60% global market share in 2021 and expand the user base more towards the luxury, professional, and fitness segments. We believe that adding smart interactions and adaptive audio filters alone will already expand our user base by 15%. With the new generation AirPods we aim to match at least the sound quality of our main competitor, the Sony WF-1000XM3, and include Active Noise Canceling that is also featured in Mifo, House of Marley, Bose, and Amazon Echo products. We will also obtain IPX4 sweat-resistant rating equal to Bose, House of Marley, and Amazon Echo earbuds, and aim to extend our range of colors, as seen in Urbanista and Jabra’s lifestyle products.

docs.title: Stakeholders
docs.text:
• Target group High-income upper-class professionals between the age of 20 and 45. Their personalities are determined and ambitious. The main benefits sought are recreation and self-expression.
  • Target purchaser Target group profile with special attention to Full Nest I and Full Nest II mothers.
  • Customer service Prefers easy-to-repair, recyclable product, and easy-to-fix complaints to fit with Apple’s intuitive user experience.
  • Marketing & Sales division Looks for unique selling points around the Apple Aspirer-Explorer lifestyle and user experience.
  • Retailers Prefer products that can withstand a wide range of storage conditions including variations in temperature, vibration, humidity, and atmospheric pressure, and have a strong and compact, theft, and vandalism-proof packaging.

docs.title: User Story #1: Jenna
docs.text:
Jenna is a 33-year-old executive who regularly visits a bar for lunch to blow off some steam. The bar is often loud with people, but it is paramount that she can hold business conversations over the phone there. Then again, she does not want to miss out on the atmosphere and be able to hear the waiters as well. Her new Apple wireless earphones allow her to switch instantly between a mode where she can fully focus on the phone conversation and a mode where the phone call and environmental sound are seamlessly combined. They also allow her to rapidly adjust the volume on the earbuds themselves without having to take out her phone.

Jenna occasionally visits the bar in the evenings. She is a big fan of the L.A. Lakers, and whenever they play, she streams the live footage through her phone. Her new earbuds allow her to easily switch to hearing everything around her and streaming the match commentary without having to ever take the earbuds out. She sometimes gets compliments on how stylish the earbuds look on her, and she wouldn’t want to miss out on hearing those either.

docs.title: Aspects
docs.text:
The new product design will be based on that of the AirPods with improvements based on the following requirements. The P1 - P10 is the "code" to indicate the priority of the requirement, from low to high.

  1. Producer Design
  2. 1.1 The product shall be visually easy to distinguish from existing AirPods as well as main competitors Sony WF-1000XM3, Jabra Elite, Amazon Echo Buds, Samsung Galaxy Buds, and Bose SoundSport Free, and Urbanista Stockholm. (P10)
  3. 1.1 The product shall be easy to recognize as an Apple product without needing a logo on its exterior. (P10)

  4. 1.2. The product shall avoid styling elements from our Powerbeats over-ear wireless headphones since those address a different market segment. (P8)

  5. Functionality

    • 2.1 The product shall incorporate one or more optical proximity sensors to detect the user wearing it. (P10)
    • 2.2 The product shall offer a dual microphone in each earbud. (P10)

docs.title: Team Goals
docs.text:
List at least five shared goals that reflect a successful product with regard to EGR3X4. Focus on team / product goals that are deeper than "getting an A".

  1. To develop an outstanding product and design as a team that meets professional industry standards and the confines of the EGR 304 class.
  2. To learn about the industry ins and outs and how to navigate them successfully by using EGR 304 class as a form of industry connection.
  3. To learn how to successfully and professionally market a unique engineering product by using guidelines established in the EGR 304 class.
  4. To just overall broaden our general knowledge of the engineering industry via taking the EGR 304 class.
  5. To better our communication skills to a consequential degree in terms of marketing our product efficiently and effectively by using knowledge gained from taking the EGR 304 class.

docs.title: Meeting Coordination
docs.text:
1. What method will you use to remind yourselves of meetings (a shared calendar?)
  2. How will your team go about changing or adding meeting times?
  3. What's the preferred format for meetings (face-to-face or virtually)?
  4. Are there any other procedures that your team feels are necessary?

We've decided that our four (or more) most optimal meeting times fall between these times: 5-8 PM Tues/Thurs. We've set Tuesdays at 6PM as the time(s) when we'll meet to discuss project details and assignments.

We’ll use text messages to remind ourselves of upcoming meetings. Any changes or additions to our meeting times must be discussed with the entire group through text messages, during lecture meetups, or during a current meeting. All members must be present when making changes to ensure there are no scheduling conflicts. Our meetups can either be virtual or in person, with in person meetings being preferred.

docs.title: Roles & Responsibilities
docs.text:
Appendix Table 2: Project Roles and Duties

Role Duties Meeting leader Schedules team meetings, creates and distributes an agenda for each meeting, and runs each meeting Meeting recorder Takes minutes of each team meeting, including attendance, and records action items and to whom they are assigned Assignment leader Coordinates the team's work on a given assignment to Canvas before the due date Project monitor Tracks the team's progress relative to the project schedule (Gantt chart) and keeps team members apprised of deadlines and project status

Meeting leader - Jacob

Meeting recorder - Troy

Assignment leader - Herman

Project monitor - Carlos

Project roles will change every other week by rotating schedule with each member moving down to the role below their current and the bottom going back up to the top. Team members will advocate for themselves in extenuating circumstances when team roles produce a conflict of interest, and the team will agree upon how to resolve such instances internally. Additionally, technical responsibilities will be distributed according to each member’s strengths, and milestones will be recorded via the project schedule.

docs.title: Conflict Recognition & Resolution
docs.text: Controversies are normal and an inherent part of team activities. The best course of action in these cases is to just simply discuss within the team members to determine the best compromise possible. If conflict cannot be resolved, then the professor will become involved to have the final say on the matter. Conflicts of interest should be discussed as soon as they arise and the team shall decide how to ease the duties of affected members
